entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Supplementary affidavit filed today by learned counsel for applicant is taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for State and perused the record.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that she is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
She has committed no offence.
Applicant was granted anticipatory bail during investigation of the case.

Further submitted that She was Manager of Rudra Pratap Polytechnic, Deorpur, Kamalpur, Sagadi, Azamgarh and allegation against her is that she obtained recognition of polytechnic college on the basis of forged papers though there is nothing on record to show that any kind of forgery was committed by the applicant.
Applicant is suffering with physical ailment and criminal history against her has been explained through supplementary affidavit.
The Vandana Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136175446/

entities.text: Vandana Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 cases shown against her as criminal history are false.
She is ready to face the trial.
There is apprehension of arrest against the applicant, so request for anticipatory bail during pendency of trial.

On the other hand, learned AGA opposed the prayer of anticipatory bail and urged that in this case during investigation material was collected on the basis of which prima facie case was found to be established against her and even inquiry was made by the Tehshildar in which allegations were found established against her.
Further urged that there is criminal history of seven case against the applicant including Gangster Act.
In this way, she is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, perusal of record, material collected during investigation and long criminal history of seven cases of similar nature, there appears no ground to grant anticipatory bail in favour of the applicant.

The anticipatory bail application of applicant Vandana Singh involved in Case Crime No. 87 of 2021,
under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, P.S. Jiyanpur, District Azamgarh is hereby rejected.

However, it is directed that in case, the applicant appears and moves bail application before the court concerned within a period of 30 days from today, it will be heard and decided expeditiously as far as possible in accordance with law.

Order Date :- 22.5.2023 A. Singh  Vandana Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136175446/
